chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Yunus ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The first of the limbs to speak on the Day of Resurrection is the womb (kinship), saying: O Lord! The one who maintained me in the world, maintain what is between You and him; and the one who cut me off in the world, cut off what is between You and him today.'
ai.seo_question: What does the womb say on the Day of Judgment regarding family ties?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the metaphysical weight of *silat al-rahim* (maintaining kinship), portraying the womb as the primary witness on the Day of Resurrection. It establishes a direct causal link between earthly familial piety and one's ultimate spiritual proximity to God, emphasizing that severing ties is not merely a social breach but a divine estrangement. This narrative reinforces the concept that ethical conduct towards relatives is a prerequisite for divine mercy and closeness.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Yunus Bin Ammar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The first one of the body parts to speak on the Day of Judgement would be the womb (i.e., kinship) saying, ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! The one maintained me in the world, so Maintain what is between You<sup>azwj</sup> and him, and the one cut me off in the world, so Cut him off today what is between You<sup>azwj</sup> and him’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn ‘Atiyah from Yunus ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘The first among the parts of human body that will speak on the Day of Judgment will be (that through which) kindred relation (comes into being). It will say, “O Lord, keep good relations with those who kept me properly in the worldly life, and cut off in this life Your good relations with those who cut me off in the worldly life.’”
